explanation: Identifier for the example sentence (S1 or S2).
The full sentence being analyzed.
Zero-based position of this token in spaCy's token sequence.
The token text (usually a word or punctuation mark).
spaCy dependency label: the grammatical relationship assigned to this token.
The token spaCy treats as this token's syntactic head.
spaCy part-of-speech label, such as NOUN, VERB, or CCONJ.
Zero-based character offset where this token starts in the sentence.
True if the lowercase token is and, but, or yet.
True if spaCy labels this token as a coordinating conjunction (cc).
Dependency label assigned to the token's head.
True if the head's dependency label is conj.
Text of the head's subtree, useful for seeing what the parser groups together.
Tokens in the head's subtree with a subject-related dependency label used by the project code.
True if at least one such subject-related token is present.
True if token is not and/but/yet OR spaCy did not label it cc.
True if the previous check passed but the head's dependency is not conj.
True if earlier checks passed but no subject-related token was found in the head subtree.
True if earlier checks passed and token is but or yet; these are handled by the separate contrast rule.
True if the token passes all checks and the code would append its character offset as a split boundary.
Plain-English guide to reading this token's diagnostic row; it is not a human-verified grammar annotation.
